correctness.rationale: Exact path component decomposition into independent truncated runs yields the full variance polynomial. For every a<c, the raw difference has coefficient signs negative, then nonnegative, then nonpositive; division by 1-p converts to cumulative coefficients with exactly one sign change. Descartes gives at most one positive root; the small-p leading coefficient and strictly convex near-p=1 square-sum establish existence and strict direction, hence simplicity. Expected outbreak ordering follows from paired geometric powers. Independent complete edge-state moment calculations matched 75 polynomials and the finite sign certificate was verified for 2,870 pairs, with no finite enumeration used as proof of the general statement.

originality.rationale: The complete pairwise and exactly-once variance-order transition was not found in the actual scholarly searches, ranked research records, or directly read related primary materials. The exact model identity is classical, but a three-region polynomial coefficient theorem supplies a distinct new all-positions statement. Past work on uniform-source path covariances, complete-bipartite variance reversals, and mean-impact reversal was compared by logical implication and does not cover the result. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete pairwise ordering phase diagram for outbreak-size uncertainty on the natural finite linear contact network, contrasting mean burden (always larger nearer the center) with variance (which always switches ranking exactly once). It is not an arbitrary finite numerical example: it holds simultaneously for every network length and every two nonreflection-equivalent seed positions, and its polynomial sign technique explains the mechanism. It can inform comparisons of seed-location risk metrics while illustrating limits of ranking by mean alone.
